summary: A first-person cybersecurity news piece argues that National Cybersecurity Strategies must be continuously improved and adapted, drawing on a September 2023 conference and interviews. It covers continuous risk assessment, public-private cooperation via the Intersect Initiative, employee awareness training, and AI/ML-based threat detection. The author concludes that repeated evaluation, collaboration, technology integration and individual empowerment are the pillars of a resilient national approach.
one_line: Opinion-style news piece arguing national cybersecurity strategies must evolve continuously through risk assessment, public-private partnership, staff training and AI.
key_facts: The author attended a conference on 8 September 2023 titled 'Adaptive Strategies for an Evolving Cyber Threat Landscape', led by Dr. Elisa Grant, a leading cybersecurity strategist.
Dr. Elisa Grant said, "National Cybersecurity Strategies (NCS) are living documents that require continuous evolution to remain effective."

Jacob Fernandez, an IT security analyst at CyberLytics, described a continuous improvement model with regular assessments, threat intelligence sharing, cross-sector collaboration and innovative technological solutions.
Jacob Fernandez compared adapting cybersecurity to combatting a virus in epidemiology: you must track mutations and adapt the vaccine accordingly.
Last year's massive data breach of the National Health Service (NHS) served as a wake-up call, and ongoing risk assessments helped the healthcare system rebound with improved defenses.
The author coins the term 'assessment inertia' for companies that fail to adjust to identified risks and so allow threats to breach their defenses.

On November 15th, 2023, the Center for Cyber Excellence launched the "Intersect Initiative", led by Amanda Zhou, bringing government agencies and private-sector companies together to build a collective defense system.
Amanda Zhou said, "Cybersecurity is not a competitive sport; a breach against one is a breach against all."
Employee Sarah McGuire thwarted a phishing attack based on instinct and training from a cybersecurity workshop provided by her employer; the author investigated this on December 13th, 2023.
On January 26, 2024, the author covered an AI-driven security protocol implemented by the Department of Finance that can discern patterns indicative of a cyberattack before human analysts would.
Tech innovator Michael Harris, who built an AI security platform, said, "Our AI can analyze millions of events per day - a volume untenable for human teams."

The article concludes that repeated evaluation, cross-sector collaboration, technological integration and individual empowerment are the cardinal points of a resilient national cybersecurity approach.
